paragraphs.text: Native Telegram bridge for Paean Harness (DeepSeek Harness distribution): chat with your agent and d
rive sessions, models, workspaces and goals from your phone. Also works with other DSH profiles.
# DSH Paean Telegram

A native **Telegram bridge for DeepSeek Harness (DSH)**, built so the **Paean Harness
distribution**

— which ships no Telegram bridge of its own — can be driven from a phone. Send a
message and the ag

ent answers in the chat; everything else (sessions, models, workspaces, goals,
skills, plugins, host
files) is one tap away on a persistent button bar.

There is **no server to run**: the plugin mounts inside the Harness Host process and talks to
the Te
legram Bot API directly over long polling.

| Package name | `dsh-telegram` (kept unchanged: profile installs reference it) |
| Version | `0.4.0

` |
| Requires | Node.js >= 22, a DSH profile (tested on Harness `0.1.0-rc.21` with `@deepseek-ai/*`

`0.2.1-alpha.1`) |
| Runtime dependency | `grammy` |
| License | MIT (see LICENSE) |

> **This repository is a fork.** It is based on
> xqicxx/dsh-telegram (MIT) and keeps the original
>

license and copyright notice. This build adds **runtime-compatibility work for the dsh 0.2.x
> host

APIs** — see Local changes in this build.
>
> **English only.** The documentation, the bot's button

labels, cards, receipts and log lines are
> all English.
>
> **Primary target: Paean Harness.** The

Paean Harness distribution ships no Telegram bridge;
> this repository exists to fill that gap. It

is developed and tested on Paean Harness
> `0.1.0-rc.21` (`@paean-ai/harness`) with `@deepseek-ai/*`

`0.2.1-alpha.1` — the combination on
> which the upstream plugin fails, see Paean Harness and
> Run

time compatibility.
>
> **Other DSH profiles: best effort, and welcome.** Nothing in the code is Pae

an-specific — it
> needs only Node.js >= 22 and the `@deepseek-ai/dsh*` peer packages — so any DSH p

rofile running
[该节后续省略]
## What you get

- **Chat with the agent**: any text you send becomes a turn for that chat's bound session.
Streaming

reasoning and tool calls appear in one message edited in place.
- **Full harness control from the p

hone**: sessions (list / resume / fork / rename / archive),
models and reasoning effort, workspaces

and the active project folder, goals, todos, the
agent inbox queue, skills, subagents, agent presets

, installed plugins, credentials
(descriptions only), host settings, background jobs, host file brow

sing, session history.
- **Turn receipts and live status**: a one-line receipt after each turn (turn

s, steps, tool
calls, tokens, cache-hit rate) and a status card that keeps refreshing while work run

s.
- **Agent tools**: the agent can send you messages and files back through the same bridge.
## Quick start
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Paean Harness

**Paean Harness** is a packaged DSH distribution (`@paean-ai/harness`) that runs a Harness process
f

rom a supervised launcher, with profiles under `~/.dsh/profiles/<name>` — for example the `web`
prof

ile that serves the Harness Web UI. It ships **no Telegram bridge**, so this plugin is
maintained to
fill exactly that gap.
### Why the upstream plugin fails on Paean

Paean's runtime bundles `@deepseek-ai/*` **0.2.1-alpha.1**, while the upstream plugin is written
aga
inst the **0.1.1-rc.2** seams. Two concrete consequences:

1. the plugin's `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` peer ranges (`^0.1.1-rc.2`) do not match the running dsh
versio

n, so the install is refused unless an exact-version exemption is granted; and
2. once forced in, se

ssion reads break — `Session.events` is a *method* on 0.2.x, and iterating it
throws `session.events
is not iterable`, so the Sessions card cannot load.

This build removes both barriers: the peer ranges span `>=0.1.1-rc.2 <0.3.0`, and the session
seams
read whichever shape the host exposes.
### Compatibility matrix
| Environment | `@deepseek-ai/*` | Status |

| Paean Harness `0.1.0-rc.21` | `0.2.1-alpha.1` | **Primary target — verified live** |
| Other DSH p

rofiles | `0.1.1-rc.2` | Supported (legacy seams) |
| Other DSH profiles | `0.2.x` | Best effort — s

ame seams as Paean |
| DSH `0.3.x` and later | — | Untested; seam work may be needed |
## Security model

- **Token**: read from the environment or a `chmod 600` file; never written by the plugin, never
ech

oed into chats or logs.
- **Inbound**: chat-id roster only; an empty roster rejects all. Optional on

e-tap bootstrap,
disabled with `security.selfAllow: false`.
- **Filesystem**: `/ls`, `/mkdir`, `/ope

n` and workspace creation can be confined with
`security.browseRoots`; attachment sending is confine

d to the workspace root.
- **Credentials**: only descriptions are ever listed — never secret values.
## Runtime compatibility

This build targets **dsh 0.2.x Host APIs** while still accepting the older 0.1.x shapes, so one
buil
d runs on both. The seams that moved:
| Seam | 0.1.1-rc.2 (older) | 0.2.x (current) |

| Live session log | `session.events` (array) | `session.snapshotEvents()` (method) |
| Event timest

amp | event `.at` | event `.time` |
| Persisted roster | `persistence.list()` → `{ id, cwd }` | `lis

t()` → `{ header, revision }` |
| Reading a cold log | `persistence.readRaw(id)` | `open(id, "read")

header, revision }` |
| Reading a cold log | `persistence.readRaw(id)` | `open(id, "read").read()` |
Notes:

- On a 0.2.x host, reading `.events` yields the *method*, and iterating it throws
`session.events is

not iterable` — the failure this fork fixes. See
Troubleshooting.
- `snapshotEvents()` is marked de

precated by dsh ("new calls prohibited") and is used here as the
only synchronous accessor; the long

-term migration is an event-driven fold.
- **Peer ranges** (`>=0.1.1-rc.2 <0.3.0` for every `@deepse

ek-ai/dsh*` peer) satisfy the
harness's compatibility gate on both generations, so installing on a 0

.2.x runtime no longer
requires an exact-version exemption.
- `/sessionlog` follows the moved export

seam: it probes `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-log-export`
first (reading the root log through `readSess

ionLogText`) and falls back to the legacy
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-host-apiproxy` module with its `readRaw`

read.
- The button labels, cards, receipts and log lines are English; the Chinese UI strings inheri

ted
from upstream were replaced throughout `src/` and `test/`.
